stories.headline: A short walk after meals can help
stories.caption: Just a few minutes of gentle walking after eating helps the body handle sugar from food.
stories.body: Taking a short, easy walk after a meal can help your body manage the sugar from your food. Researchers have found that even two to five minutes of light movement makes a difference compared with sitting still. It does not need to be fast or long. A stroll around the block, walking the dog or tidying up the kitchen all count. General information, not medical advice.
keyFacts: Two to five minutes can help
stories.whyTrending: An easy habit almost anyone can try today

quiz.statement: A walk must last an hour to help after a meal.

stories.headline: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
stories.caption: Two hearts pump blood through the gills while the third sends it around the rest of the body.
stories.body: Octopuses are even stranger than they look. Each one has three hearts. Two of them push blood through the gills, where it picks up oxygen, and the third pumps it around the body. Their blood is blue because it uses copper rather than iron to carry oxygen. That copper-based blood works well in cold ocean water with little oxygen.
stories.whyTrending: One of nature’s most surprising body plans

stories.headline: Honey found in ancient tombs was still edible
stories.caption: Archaeologists have found pots of honey thousands of years old that had never spoiled.
stories.body: Honey is one of the few foods that can last almost forever. Archaeologists exploring ancient Egyptian tombs have found pots of honey that were thousands of years old and still had not spoiled. Honey has very little water and is naturally acidic, which makes it very hard for germs to grow. Bees also add an enzyme that helps protect it.
stories.whyTrending: A sticky mystery with a scientific answer

quiz.statement: Honey spoils after a few months.

stories.headline: A day on Venus outlasts its year
stories.caption: Venus spins so slowly that one day there is longer than the time it takes to circle the Sun.
stories.body: Venus is a planet of extremes. It turns very slowly, taking about 243 Earth days to spin around once. But it only takes about 225 Earth days to travel all the way around the Sun. That means a single day on Venus lasts longer than its whole year. It also spins in the opposite direction to most planets, so the Sun rises in the west.
keyFacts: The Sun rises in the west
stories.whyTrending: Our neighbour planet breaks the usual rules

quiz.statement: On Venus the Sun rises in the west.

stories.headline: Why yawning is contagious
stories.caption: Seeing or even reading about a yawn can trigger one, and scientists think it is linked to empathy.
stories.body: Have you yawned yet? Yawning is famously catching. Seeing someone yawn, hearing it or even reading about it can set you off. Scientists think contagious yawning may be linked to how people connect with each other, because we tend to catch yawns more from friends and family than from strangers. Yawning may also help cool the brain. General information, not medical advice.
keyFacts: Reading about yawns can trigger one
Caught more from people we know
stories.whyTrending: Did you yawn reading this headline?

quiz.statement: You catch yawns more easily from strangers.

stories.headline: Wombats make cube-shaped droppings
stories.caption: The Australian animal is the only one known to produce square poos, and scientists have worked out why.
stories.body: Wombats are famous for something unusual: their droppings come out shaped like little cubes. Scientists studied how it happens and found that the walls of a wombat’s gut are stretchy in some places and stiffer in others, which shapes the droppings as they form. Wombats stack them on rocks and logs, possibly to mark their territory and talk to other wombats.

quiz.statement: Wombat droppings are shaped like cubes.

Real stories will replace this soon.

quiz.statement: The cooking school charges a fee.

stories.headline: Bananas are berries but strawberries are not
stories.caption: In plant science a berry grows from one flower with seeds inside, which rules strawberries out.
stories.body: Here is a fruit fact to surprise your friends. To botanists, a berry is a fruit that grows from a single flower and has its seeds inside. By that rule, bananas, grapes and even tomatoes are berries. Strawberries are not, because their tiny seeds sit on the outside. Raspberries do not count either, since each one is made of many small fruits joined together.
stories.whyTrending: A fruit bowl full of surprises

stories.headline: Town elects a cat as honorary mayor
stories.caption: Residents of a small town voted a friendly local cat as honorary mayor, and it greets visitors daily.
stories.body: Some towns choose unusual leaders. Over the years, several small communities have named animals as honorary mayors, including cats, dogs and even a goat. The roles are just for fun and often help raise money for animal charities. One famous cat mayor greeted tourists at a local shop every day for years and became a popular attraction in its own right.
keyFacts: Honorary roles are just for fun
Cats, dogs and a goat have served
stories.whyTrending: Proof that small towns have big personalities

quiz.statement: Animal mayors often help raise money for charity.

stories.headline: Your brain uses a fifth of your energy
stories.caption: Although it is only about 2% of body weight, the brain burns around 20% of the energy you use.
stories.body: Your brain is a hungry organ. It makes up only about two percent of your body weight, yet it uses roughly twenty percent of the energy your body burns each day. That energy powers billions of nerve cells sending signals to each other. Regular meals, sleep and staying hydrated all help your brain do its job. General information, not medical advice.
keyFacts: Sleep and water help it work
stories.whyTrending: A fact that makes a great excuse for breakfast

quiz.statement: The brain uses about 20% of the body’s energy.

questions.headline: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
questions.question: Octopus blood is blue because it uses which metal?
questions.explanation: Copper carries oxygen in octopus blood and turns it blue — it works well in cold, low-oxygen seas.

questions.headline: Wombats make cube-shaped droppings
questions.question: Wombats are native to which country?
questions.explanation: Wombats live only in Australia, where they dig long burrows to sleep in during the day.

questions.headline: A day on Venus outlasts its year
questions.question: Venus is the hottest planet, but which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is closest, but Venus is hotter because its thick clouds trap heat like a blanket.

questions.headline: Bananas are berries but strawberries are not
questions.question: Botanically speaking, which of these counts as a berry?
questions.explanation: A banana grows from a single flower with its seeds inside, so botanists call it a berry.

questions.headline: Honey found in ancient tombs was still edible
questions.question: What is a group of honey bees living together called?
questions.explanation: Honey bees live in colonies, and one colony can hold tens of thousands of bees.

questions.headline: Your brain uses a fifth of your energy
questions.question: Which part of your body protects your brain?
questions.explanation: Your skull is a strong shell of bones that keeps your hard-working brain safe.
